answer: Anti-sybil design binds each identity to a scarce anchor. A verifier issues a one-time cipher challenge that only a uniquely attested device can solve, so cloning accounts is not free. Like cracking many walnut shells, each fake identity still burns real time and money. A lotus reputation score opens only after sustained honest work, not a burst of signups. An attacker chasing thousands of votes must buy or forge that many anchors, paying hardware, gas, and opportunity cost that scales linearly, while honest users pay once. That asymmetry blunts sybil floods without locking out real people.
